chunks: Designing a PCB for testing. The question: How can you design a PCB for testing?
Designing a board for testing means you can both set up and observe what is happening inside it. You do that for the factory and for yourself at the bench.
In practice you add test pads on the important signals, a connector to program and debug the chip, and ways to power and measure one block at a time.
Think of a house built with access panels and windows into the walls.
The plumber can check each pipe without tearing out plaster, and can shut off the water to one room to test it.
A board needs the same two things: places to look (observe) and ways to switch parts on or off (control). The analogy has one catch.
Every opening costs space, and on fast signals even a tiny pad can disturb the signal.
A DFT plan has four threads. Each maps to concrete layout and schematic features you can show in an interview.
Test point: a pad, loop or via (a small plated hole) where a probe can touch a signal. Observability: the ability to measure what a node (one point in the circuit) is doing.
Controllability: the ability to force a node into a known state. Boundary scan: using the chips' built-in pin controls to test connections you cannot probe.
Zero-ohm link: a tiny jumper in a supply line that you can remove or replace to isolate or measure that block.
Put a 10 milliohms shunt, which is a small known resistor, in the supply line of one block, with test pads across it.
If the block draws 2 amps, the voltage across the shunt is 2 amps x 10 milliohms = 20 millivolts, so measuring 20 millivolts tells you the current.
The power lost is 2 amps x 20 millivolts = 40 milliwatts, small enough to ignore. That is the whole idea.
"Design for test means building in controllability and observability.

I give each rail, clock, reset and key signal a test pad with a nearby ground, add programming and debug connectors, series jumpers so I can power and measure blocks separately, and test modes, loopbacks or boundary scan in firmware and silicon.
For the factory I put pads on one side at fixture-friendly size and pitch. I prioritise by risk and keep fast nets clean."
